heroHeadline: IAEA Confirms Drone Strike on Zaporizhzhia NPP Turbine Hall; Ukraine Hits Saratov Refinery + Kirov Pipeline Station; Russia Strikes Kharkiv, Odesa, Chernihiv — 229 Combat Clashes
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,558 (June 1, 2026), the IAEA issued Update 307 confirming a drone struck the turbine hall next to reactor unit 6 at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant — first attack within the ZNPP perimeter since April 2024. IAEA DG Grossi warned 'attacks on nuclear sites are unacceptable'; radiation levels remain normal. Ukraine denied responsibility, accusing Russia of staging the incident before the June IAEA Board of Governors session. Overnight (May 31 → June 1), Ukraine launched 229 long-range drones: the Rosneft Saratov oil refinery was set ablaze (~700 km from the front), and the Lazarevo pumping station in Kirov region was struck (~1,300 km from Ukraine) — serving the Surgut-Gorky-Polotsk pipeline. Russia claimed to intercept 216 drones; Ukraine's air force confirmed 212 downed. Russia struck Kharkiv (two districts; garages and vehicles on fire), Odesa (two floors of residential building partially destroyed; 1 injured), Chernihiv (40,000 electricity customers cut), and Dnipropetrovsk (4 injured). On the frontline: 229 combat clashes; Pokrovsk sector repelled 40 Russian assault attempts, destroying 50+ Russian soldiers. Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,365,470 personnel (+1,410 in 24 hours). Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck 18 Russian oil facilities throughout May 2026 — the most intense energy infrastructure campaign of the war.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Defense News, Euronews, Euromaidan Press, Soufan Center, Meduza, United24 Media, RBC Ukraine, Washington Times, empr.media, Militarnyi, Kyiv Post, Japan Times, NBC News, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
